## Plugin reference

- Description: The shared tag picker: TagPickerPanel (pure — search or create a typed path, the foldable tree with rolled-up counts, inline create and rename, a ⋯ menu to recolour, nest out and delete, whole-row drag to reorder and nest), TagPickerPopover wiring it to a declared tree or to any other backend (a TagPickerSource: rows, writes, and the TagPickerAbilities it has — manual order, icons, shading, its colour palette, clearing a colour — so the picker offers only what the backend can do; without writes the panel is a read-only picking tree), the TagPathChip header chip and TagMark.

## `TagPickerPanel`

Pure: the rows and the writes in, picks out. An empty query is the foldable
tree (hover ＋ and ⋯, double-click to rename, drag to reorder or nest, "New
tag" at the foot); a query lists every tag whose path holds it and offers to
create the typed path.

The ⋯ menu (`TagRowMenu`): Rename · Add sub-tag · Icon… (the Material
Symbols picker, in a control panel anchored on the ⋯ as the menu closes) ·
Move out of the parent · Shade children (a parent's `childColors: "ramp"`) ·
the colour swatches (led by "Same as parent", or "No colour" on a root) · the caller's `rowMenuExtra` · Delete (immediate; hidden
where `canDelete` says no).

Two shapes of use, one component:

- **A carrier's picker** (the defaults — `TagPickerPopover`): a trailing ✓ on
  `selected`, every tag unfolded, the search focused, a created path picked.
- **A filter** (Places' sidebar): `indicator="checkbox"` draws a leading box
  — ✓ `selected`, − `negated` (the name struck through), and a primary − on
  every ancestor of either (derived, never passed);
  `defaultExpanded="roots"`, `autoFocus={false}`, `pickCreated={false}` (a
  new tag carries nothing, so picking it would filter everything out).
- **A navigation tree** (Mail's sidebar labels): `indicator="none"` (the
  open view's tag only highlighted), `search={false}`, `fadeEmpty={false}`
  (the counts are an unread badge, not carriers), `countsOf="own"` (each
  label's own unread, a folded label the total under it), `marks="flat"`
  (every label one full dot of the colour it shows in — no faded inherited
  dot, no dashed "no colour" ring), `noun="label"` ("New label", "Add
  sub-label").

## Backends that are not a tag tree

`TagPickerPopover` takes a declared `tree`, or a `source`
(`TagPickerSource`): `read`, a `ResourceResult` of its rows and its
`TagPickerAbilities` (`TagPickerBackend` — abilities may hang on a read too:
Mail's palette is the account's), and its writes (`TagPickerWrites`). The rows are `TagPickerRow`s (what the picker reads:
id, name, parent, colour, child shading, icon, rank), which a `TagRow` is.
`closeOnPick={false}` keeps it open across picks (a carrier of many tags).

The abilities make the picker offer only what the backend can do, never fake
it (a declared tree has all of them, `TAG_TREE_ABILITIES`):

- `reorder` off: no before/after drop zones — a drag only nests, and siblings
  stay in the rows' `rank` order (Gmail labels, sorted by name);
- `icons` off: no Icon…; `shadeChildren` off: no Shade children;
- `palette`: the swatches (Gmail's label palette); `inheritColor` off: no
  "Same as parent" / "No colour" (the colour cannot be cleared).

Without `writes` the panel is a **read-only picking tree** (no ＋, ⋯,
rename, drag, create or "New tag") — the standard tags cell editor's, over a
field's options (`tagRowsOfOptions`, the inverse of `tagFieldOptions`).

A row whose `counts` entry is 0 draws its name faint (unless `fadeEmpty` is
false). The panel's root carries
`data-tag-picker`; its rows are the tree primitive's `[data-tree-id]`.
